newsitem.title: USA: ASA, USFGC seek to boost Brazil hog production.
newsitem.headline: ASA, USFGC seek to boost Brazil hog production.

text.p: The American Soybean Association (ASA) and the U.S. Feed Grains Council (USFGC) will hire a consultant to oversee a swine technical program in Brazil and encourage expansion of pork production.

Brazil is the leading competitor of the United States in exports of soybeans and soy products. Brazil's pork production is also the largest in Latin America and is forecast to grow to 2 million tonnes a year in 2000 from 1.4 million in 1995.
The U.S. agribusiness groups said they expect an additional 3.9 million tonnes of increased feedgrain demand in Brazil due to planned hog industry expansion.

"Since Brazil is our biggest competitor for international markets, we would like to see their domestic consumption of soybeans and soyproducts grow significantly," said Arno Partner, ASA director for Latin America. "Swine production represents a great opportunity for immediate returns."
The consultant will advise on Brazil's hog and grain production and also promote the use of U.S. grains.
